Twyne acts without being asked. The buttons remain, but as shortcuts rather
than the way work starts.

The same digest goes along when you _do_ press **Get notes**, so the deliberate

### The rubric grades against _this_ piece

The default signed-in check first attempts one typed judgement over the enabled
criteria, including custom criteria. The editors then read each new version on
their own, at most once every ten minutes, in the background so the grade stays
on screen. Their notes survive later quick checks and say when they are about
an earlier version. **Ask them now** reads the current version straight away;
Twyne also takes the room path when the quick check is unavailable.

In the room reading, the static feature scorer measures shape — sentence-length variance,

That path’s **Target Fit** judge scores relevance independently of craft, and caps
every shape-derived criterion by it. Lowering target fit can only ever lower
the grade, never raise it.

The criteria themselves are yours to shape. Twyne ships a fixed spine so a

and a second "by your weights" score appears beside the editorial grade. Every
pass is recorded, so the panel shows the run of grades rather than a snapshot.

# Autonomous editorial work — change summary

Responds to the Twyne UX improvement brief of 2026-10-19 and to
the product direction that followed it: **Twyne acts without being asked.**
Reviews, research and editors' readings run on their own; buttons remain as
shortcuts and overrides, not as the way work starts.

Released in 0.25.0.

## Principle

A feature that waits for a click before doing its core job is a defect. Each
automatic path has a trigger (folio open, draft change, idle pause, a fresh
quick grade) and spend guards (rate floors, session caps, dedupe by draft
fingerprint). Empty states say what Twyne is about to do, not what to press.
Hosted writers without their own model get the automatic path too.

## 1. Review and research arrive on their own

### Background room — `src/utils/background-room.ts`

| Before                                                                                          | After                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Existing prose counted as read on every open, so an unread draft was never read until Get notes | What the room last read is stored per folio (`background-room-read:<folioId>`). A folio with no record and no notes starts empty and is read on its own; one with notes from before the record existed counts as read |
| Triggered by 500 **net** new words and a 2-minute pause                                         | Triggered by 200 words in new or rewritten paragraphs (`diffParagraphs(...).added`) and a 1-minute pause                                                                                                              |
| `startBackgroundRoom` had no current draft                                                      | `currentText` arms the watcher straight away when the draft holds unread work                                                                                                                                         |

Guards unchanged: `MIN_INTERVAL_MS` (5 min), `MAX_PASSES_PER_SESSION` (8),
`MIN_EDITOR_WORDS` (500) before any reading. `src/routes/editor/index.tsx`
loads the stored baseline and existing notes when the folio opens.

### Rubric — `src/components/rubric/rubric-panel.tsx`

- `autoReadRoom` starts the editors' reading when a live-review quick grade
  arrives for a draft fingerprint the editors have not read, at most every
  `ROOM_READ_FLOOR_MS` (10 min, stored per folio), and only when a hosted
  client or BYOK provider exists.
- `runAnalysis(frontierOnly, quiet)` — a quiet run uses `isReviewing`, so the
  current grade stays on screen instead of the full-panel loader.
- The editors' notes survive later quick checks (`judges` carried forward);
  `judgesFingerprint` marks notes about an earlier version. A reading whose
  draft changed mid-run keeps its notes rather than discarding them.
- Automatic readings snapshot as `automatic` (5-minute spacing) so they cannot
  crowd manual checkpoints out of the 50-entry history; requested readings
  still force a `rubric` checkpoint.
- The Editors tab says `soon` / `reading…` instead of `0`.

### Research — `src/utils/background-research.ts`, `src/utils/research-candidates.ts` (new)

- Hosted writers without their own model: `claimCandidates` finds figures,
  attributed quotations, appeals to authority and dated events by rule;
  one batched Jev request (`candidateRequest`) confirms which need a source
  (Noul ≥ 0.6), with fiction instructed to ignore invented events.
- `ResearchIdleReason` (`waiting`, `too-short`, `no-provider`, `no-claims`,
  `covered`, `pass-done`) replaces the bare "Watching draft".
- Failed passes and failed claims retry on their own at 30 s, 2 min and
  10 min (`scheduleRetry`), then stop and leave the retry control.
- Each Deep trace row says what found / no match / failed means and offers
  Go to the claim.

## 2. Passage grounding and card meaning

- **Quotations** — `src/utils/quote-grounding.ts` (new). `extractQuotations`
  reads paired quotation marks and Markdown block quotes; `resolveQuotation`
  normalises typography, case and whitespace, follows `…` elisions within one
  paragraph, never crosses paragraphs, and breaks ties with the note's
  surrounding words (same paragraph only, stopwords removed). Ties stay
  `ambiguous`; missing text stays `unmatched`. `renderGroundedMarkdown` wraps
  resolved quotations as links after safe Markdown rendering. Links are
  re-resolved on `twyne:content` and again in the editor on click
  (`twyne:reveal-quote`, `findQuotationRange`). Used by the Cast panel notes
  and replies and the in-manuscript note card.
- **Relationship cards** — `flow-conductor.ts` asks a Choice alongside the echo
  Noul (`ECHO_RELATIONS`); shared vocabulary only suppresses the card. The card
  shows both passages and offers That's the connection / Not how I read it.
- **Settled notes** — `src/utils/note-decisions.ts` (new). Intentional / later
  per note, stored on this device (`note-decisions:<folioId>`). A decision
  stands while its anchor still resolves in the draft; `withoutSettled` drops
  repeat notes from the same editor in explicit and background passes, and
  `decisionsDigest` goes to the editors as context.

## 3. Versions — `src/utils/revision-history.ts`, `version-history-panel.tsx`

- `describeRevision` writes one sentence per comparison from the changes
  (rewrote / cut / added, and whose notes the rewrites reached).
- Changes are labelled Rewritten / Cut / New passage with Before and After.
- `notesTouchedBy` shows editor notes whose anchor was in the old passage and
  is gone from the new one — evidence the change reached the note, not proof
  it answered it.
- Optional intent on Save checkpoint (`RevisionSnapshot.intent`) names the
  checkpoint. Counts move under Size of the change.

## Answers to the brief's open questions

- **Cast cards / "further on as you read".** Cast cards are `PersonasPanel`
  notes (`personas-panel.tsx`); the "Further on in this piece" card is an
  `echo` flow item from `flow-conductor.ts`, rendered by `flow-surface.tsx`.
- **Editor review and the manual click.** The quick check never runs the
  editors; the click started their reading. It now starts on its own.
- **"Watching graph".** Research went idle silently when there was no
  provider, the draft was short, no claims were found or all were covered.
  Each is now a named state, and hosted writers have a provider path.
- **Jev's decisions.** Jev confirms echo relevance and relationship, hosted
  research claims, note quality gates, and the quick grade; the relationship

I found two separate problems. First, the default search route has no backend on prod, so the loop is actually blocked. Second, even with search working, the loop is a single search per sentence with nothing that reads or checks what comes back. I worked this out from the code and the Convex env vars; I didn't run the app.

## 1. Why it looks blocked

Everyone starts on `researchProvider: "hosted"` (`src/types/index.ts:1149`), which sends every search to `api.research.searchSources`.

- **Prod is missing the setting.** It has `NOTORGANIC_ENABLED=true` but no `RESEARCH_PROVIDER` and no `RESEARCH_API_KEY`. With nothing set, `providerId()` falls back to TinyFish with an empty key (`convex/research.ts:215`), so `liveSearchConfigured()` is false and you get the local stub.
- **The stub becomes a failure on every claim.** `src/utils/background-research.ts:815` turns it into "Live research is not configured. Choose a research provider in Settings…". So the loop finds claims, and then each one fails.
- **Your own AI model doesn't help.** Your model picks the claims, but the search still goes through the hosted route unless you switched to model web search, a search API or MCP in Settings.
- **Local dev always gets stubs.** The dev deployment has no research or Not Organic variables at all.

The fix was already written and never turned on. The comment at `convex/research.ts:368` describes this exact failure: "an Apparatus that never finds a source". The fix is `RESEARCH_PROVIDER=notorganic`, which searches through the writer's linked Not Organic account. It depends on the gateway's `/v1/web/search`, which was returning 502 on Oct 23 because of a stale Keenable key. The Oct 28 gateway deploy should have loaded the new key, but I haven't checked that it did.

## 2. Why it wouldn't match your vision even when it works

Here is what one pass does today:

- **Claim finding (hosted users):** four regexes look for figures, attributed quotes, "studies show" and "in 19xx". Jev then says yes or no to each match (`src/utils/research-candidates.ts`). A named person, a book, a place or a period detail in a novel never matches.
- **The search query is the sentence itself**, cut to 180 characters. Search engines handle that poorly.
- **One search per claim.** A miss is marked done and never retried with a different query in that session (`background-research.ts:554`).
- **It never reads a source.** `fetchSource` exists in Convex, but nothing in `src/` calls it.
- **"Found" only means the search returned something.** Ranking scores snippet length, author, publisher and position (`src/utils/research-targets.ts:373`). Nothing checks that the page supports the claim. The Clairic value-support check exists, but only in the evals.
- **Hard caps:** 5 claims per pass and 25 background sources per folio. After that it stops.
- **It only reacts to sentences already in the draft.** It never researches the Dossier's subject on its own.

If you meant the native GPUI build: its Apparatus has no research transport at all. The parity fixtures mark those captures "blocked" for that reason.

## What I'd do

1. **Unblock it.** Check that gateway search answers, then set `RESEARCH_PROVIDER=notorganic` on prod. Also change `providerId()` to use Not Organic whenever it's enabled and no key is set, so this can't quietly break again. Each search charges the writer's wallet, up to the $0.05 ceiling.
2. **Make it an actual research loop.** For each claim:
   - The model writes a few queries, searches, and fetches the top pages.
   - Clairic or Jev judges each page: supports, contradicts or unrelated.
   - If nothing supports the claim, it rewrites the queries and tries again, within a budget.
   - It saves only sources that support the claim, along with the passage that does. A contradicting source becomes a fact-check note.
   - Hosted claim finding moves from the regexes to Clairic extraction, which already runs through Not Organic.

The gap is closed. A source now goes on file only if a passage from it says what the claim says. The changes aren't committed, and the new code isn't on prod yet.

**How each claim is researched now** (`resolveClaim` in `src/utils/background-research.ts`, helpers in `src/utils/research-verify.ts`):
1. **Several queries per claim, up to three.** Hosted claims search on the key terms first ("1903 Wright brothers flew first powered aircraft Kitty Hawk"), not the raw sentence. A model's own query stays first, and quotations are also searched as the exact phrase.
2. **Reads the top three hits** from each search:
   - Signed-in writers: through Not Organic's page fetch. I checked it live: it read the Wright Flyer page from Wikipedia, about 30,000 characters.
   - Writers with their own Keenable key: through Keenable directly.
   - Other search keys can't fetch pages, so those claims are judged on the search snippet.
3. **Takes the passage that matters.** That's the paragraphs that share the claim's names and figures.
4. **Judges each source:** supports, contradicts or unrelated. Being on the same topic doesn't count as support. Jev judges for signed-in writers and your own model otherwise.
5. **If nothing supports the claim, it tries the next query.** A contradicting source is saved and flagged. Search hits that support nothing are no longer saved.
6. **Rate limits pause it instead of failing it.** It waits the "Try again in Ns" the server gives, then continues.

**In the UI:**
- Each claim shows what it's doing live: "search 2 of 3", "reading nps.gov", "checking 3 sources".
- Settled claims read "2 supports", "contradicted" (in red) or "unsourced".
- Saved sources are stamped "supports" or "contradicts" and quote the passage, in place of the old "why:" line.
- The Deep Trace text says what was done, for example "Searched 3 ways and read 6 pages; nothing said what this claim says".

**Local dev:** the dev deployment now uses Keenable with the key from skate. I pushed the Convex code there and a dev search returned real results.

**Checks:**
- New end-to-end tests for the loop pass. They cover trying a second query after a miss, keeping a contradiction flagged, and never filing unrelated hits.
- I also added unit tests for the queries, passage picking, verdicts and the Not Organic page fetch. Both typechecks pass.
- I haven't run it in the browser.
- The two failing `personas-panel.tsx` tests are unchanged.

**Costs:**
- **Spend:** on the account route each claim can now cost up to 3 searches plus 9 page reads on the writer's Not Organic credit, where it used to be one search. In practice it stops at the first supporting source.
- **Speed:** free-tier writers are limited to 5 searches a minute, so a full pass can now take a few minutes. It waits; it doesn't fail.

# Deploying Twyne

Twyne ships as a Qwik City SSR app. The browser bundle is built by Vite into
`dist/`, the SSR server entry into `server/`, and `server.js` (Node `http`)
serves both and listens on `$PORT`.

## Railway (primary)

The repo is configured for [Railway](https://railway.com) via `railway.json`
(`builder: RAILPACK`) and [`railpack.json`](https://railpack.com) — Railpack is
Railway's successor to Nixpacks:

- **Install** (Bun): `bun install --frozen-lockfile`
- **Build** (Bun): `bash scripts/railway-build.sh` — runs Convex deploy + Vite
  client + Vite SSR server. If `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY` is unset, the script
  degrades to a frontend-only build (backend left untouched).
- **Start** (Node): `node server.js`
- **Healthcheck**: `GET /`

> The `build` step is auto-generated by Railpack from the Node provider
> (uses the mise step to install `bun` + `node`, then runs
> `bun install --frozen-lockfile`). We only override the `build` step to
> inject the Convex deploy + Vite build via `scripts/railway-build.sh` —
> the script is required because the inline `if/then/else` with nested
> single-quoted `&&` strings gets mangled by the build step's shell
> serialization.

`railpack.json` pins `node: 20` + `bun: 1` so the runtime image has `node`
available for the start command (`server.js` uses `node:http`), while Bun does
the install and Vite build.

### One-time setup

1. **Create / link the service** (already linked to `Diogenesoftoronto/twyne`):

   ```bash
   railway add --service twyne --repo Diogenesoftoronto/twyne
   ```

   Railway auto-deploys on every push to the connected branch.

2. **Set environment variables** (see `.env.example` for the full list). The
   `VITE_*` values are baked in at build time, so they must be set on the
   service before the first build:

   ```bash
   railway variables \
     --set "CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY=prod:your-deployment|..." \
     --set "VITE_CONVEX_URL=https://your-deployment.convex.cloud" \
     --set "VITE_CONVEX_SITE_URL=https://your-deployment.convex.site" \
     --set "BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=..." \
     --set "BETTER_AUTH_URL=https://www.twyne.love" \
     --set "SITE_URL=https://www.twyne.love"
   ```

   `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY` is the production **deploy key** from the Convex
   dashboard (Settings → Deploy keys). The build step uses it to push the
   backend; without it the build only ships the frontend. `PORT` is injected by
   Railway automatically — do not set it.

3. **Custom domain**: in the Railway service → Settings → Networking, add
   `www.twyne.love` and point the DNS `CNAME` at the generated Railway target.
   Until the domain resolves, auth callbacks that expect `https://www.twyne.love`
   will not complete — use the `*.up.railway.app` URL or temporarily set
   `BETTER_AUTH_URL`/`SITE_URL` to it while testing.

### Convex in production

`VITE_CONVEX_URL` should point at a **production** Convex deployment, not a dev
one. The Railway build now runs `npx convex deploy` (gated on `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY`)
as part of the build step, so the backend deploys on every push alongside the
frontend — no separate manual deploy needed.

Sign-in is through Not Organic. ATProto is a separate publishing connection;

  echo "==> Deploying Convex backend"
